analysis_notes.gap_explanation: Torah #187 is a five-line teaching with zero bechina edges in torahData.js (the reference field 187 does not appear in the dataset at all). The source text uses the word 'bechinot' explicitly in line 3: 'ארץ היינו בחינות ארץ ישראל, היא מתקוממה לו' — 'the earth, that is the aspect/bechina of Eretz Israel, rises up against him'. This declaration equates the general word 'ארץ' in the Job verse with the specific concept of ארץ ישראל, meaning they share the same essential nature in this teaching — a genuine bechina relationship. A second bechina is present in lines 1-2: the teaching opens by calling mida-k'neged-mida itself a 'chesed gadol' (great kindness), meaning chesed and mida-k'neged-mida are two expressions of the same divine quality here — not cause and effect, but parallel aspects of the same reality. A third structural equation appears in line 4: the acronym of 'ארץ אוכלת יושביה' spelling 'אתה תשלם לאיש כמעשהו' equates the 'devouring earth' with the measure-for-measure principle. These three bechina relationships — (1) ארץ ↔ ארץ ישראל, (2) חסד ↔ מדה כנגד מדה, (3) ארץ אוכלת יושביה ↔ מדה כנגד מדה — are all present in the source text but absent from the dataset. The eight concepts listed above are candidates for future bechina-edge additions when Torah #187 is formally encoded into torahData.js.
analysis_notes.source_text_summary: Torah 187 (Psalms 62:13) teaches: The verse 'And to You, God, is chesed, for You pay each person according to their deeds' reveals that measure-for-measure is itself a great chesed — because through it a person comes to examine their deeds, recognize the sin they committed, and do teshuva. However, this precise measure-for-measure repayment operates primarily in Eretz Israel, as the verse in Job (20:27) says: 'The heavens will reveal his iniquity, and the earth will rise up against him' — the 'earth' here is the bechina (aspect) of Eretz Israel, where sin is disclosed, because there divine precision in repayment is at its greatest. This is further proven by the verse about Eretz Israel in Numbers (13:32): 'ארץ אוכלת יושביה' (the land that devours its inhabitants) — whose acronym (aleph-tav-lamed-kaf) spells 'אתה תשלם לאיש כמעשהו' (You pay each person according to their deeds), confirming the identity of the two principles. Therefore, those dwelling in Eretz Israel typically have much suffering, because there God applies measure-for-measure swiftly.
